repair_note: Core frameworks were rewritten to remove slogan-like language and expose decisions, operating conditions, tradeoffs, misuse risks, and source traceability.
core_thesis: Operational excellence is reimagined as an integrated operating capability: operations must support marketing promises, customer value, and stakeholder impact through QCDS and the CI-EL / PI-PM capability clusters.

core_frameworks.what_it_is: A holistic entrepreneurial-marketing architecture that treats operations as the center of gravity rather than a back-office function.
core_frameworks.source_specific_meaning: The book places operations in the Omnihouse foundation: marketing promises, customer value, and stakeholder outcomes must be supported by QCDS capability and by the CI-EL / PI-PM capability clusters.
how_components_interact: Marketing ZEN and entrepreneurial ambition create promises; QCDS tests whether operations can fulfill them.
CI-EL stretches what the organization can attempt; PI-PM turns ambition into repeatable execution.
Stakeholder orientation expands operational excellence beyond internal efficiency and customer satisfaction.
core_frameworks.business_decision_improved: Which operating capability must be strengthened before the business expands its market promise or stakeholder ambition.
operating_conditions: multi-function decisions where marketing, operations, service, and leadership are interdependent
organizations moving from siloed optimization to customer or stakeholder value
situations where current operating capability limits brand promise
tradeoffs: holistic coordination can slow decisions if accountability is unclear
stakeholder ambition can exceed operational maturity
flexibility may create complexity if core QCDS disciplines are weak
risks_of_misuse: using Omnihouse language as a slogan without changing operating routines
treating operations as universally responsible while decision rights remain siloed
claiming stakeholder centricity without evidence of impact
diagnostic_questions: Which customer promise currently depends most on operational capability?
Where do marketing claims, QCDS performance, and stakeholder impact disagree?
Which capability cluster is weakest: CI-EL or PI-PM?

core_frameworks.what_it_is: A lens for stretching operations from efficiency and standardization toward flexibility, customer responsiveness, and stakeholder contribution.
core_frameworks.source_specific_meaning: Chapter 1 argues that operational excellence must move along a frontier rather than remain fixed at cost, conformance, and departmental targets.
how_components_interact: Baseline discipline prevents flexibility from becoming chaos.
Adaptive capability lets operations respond to customer and ecosystem changes.
Stakeholder responsibility adds boundaries: speed, cost, and service must remain conscientious.
core_frameworks.business_decision_improved: Whether to standardize, customize, automate, partner, or redesign the operating model for a given customer promise.
risks_of_misuse: stretching before the basics are reliable
mistaking many options for valuable flexibility
ignoring front-line burden created by customized promises
diagnostic_questions: Which variation creates customer value, and which variation is operational waste?
Where does flexibility depend on frontline discretion rather than designed capability?
Which nonnegotiable standard must remain stable while the service flexes?

core_frameworks.what_it_is: A staged view of quality, cost, delivery, and service maturity across divisional, company, customer, and stakeholder orientations.
core_frameworks.source_specific_meaning: Chapter 1 defines four QCDS stages: quality shifts from input to impact, cost from cutting to social contribution, delivery from on-estimate to on-conscience, and service from standardization to transformation.
how_components_interact: Each QCDS dimension can mature at a different pace.
A higher-stage claim is only credible when lower-stage operating basics are under control.
The stages help identify whether a constraint is internal, customer-facing, or stakeholder-facing.
core_frameworks.business_decision_improved: Which QCDS dimension should receive management attention before a company claims broader operational excellence.
tradeoffs: stage advancement may require new evidence and governance
customer-centric speed can conflict with stakeholder conscience
company-centric cost reduction can damage customer value
risks_of_misuse: treating the stages as a maturity badge rather than a diagnostic lens
jumping to stakeholder claims while internal failures remain unresolved
averaging QCDS into a single vague score
diagnostic_questions: Which QCDS dimension is still divisional while the strategy assumes customer centricity?
Which lower-stage discipline must be protected before moving to a higher-stage promise?
Where is stakeholder language being used without stakeholder evidence?

Stakeholder contribution asks whether efficiency releases value rather than only reducing spend.

tradeoffs: supplier cost pressure versus ecosystem resilience
risks_of_misuse: calling any cost cut operational excellence
using humanity language without changing incentives
excluding customer value from cost decisions

core_frameworks.what_it_is: A shift from promised dates and schedules toward delivery design that is reliable, responsive, technologically enabled, and ethically conscious.
core_frameworks.source_specific_meaning: Chapter 5 moves delivery from on-estimate to on-schedule, on-demand, and on-conscience, including goods, services, logistics evolution, and green considerations.
how_components_interact: Scheduling discipline supports reliability; on-demand capability adds responsiveness; on-conscience delivery adds environmental and social boundaries.
Goods and services both require delivery design, though evidence and failure modes differ.
Digital visibility helps only if promises are calibrated to actual capacity.
core_frameworks.business_decision_improved: How fast and flexible a delivery promise can be without undermining reliability, cost, customer trust, or conscience commitments.
tradeoffs: green logistics claims versus cost and current evidence
risks_of_misuse: treating tracking visibility as delivery excellence
making green delivery claims without current validation
diagnostic_questions: Which part of the customer promise depends on delivery reliability?
Where do speed claims exceed capacity evidence?
Which delivery choice has stakeholder consequences that must be made visible?

core_frameworks.what_it_is: A shift from consistent service blueprints to data-informed personalization, agile customization, and services that improve customer or societal conditions.

how_components_interact: Blueprints stabilize the basic experience; evaluation reveals where customers perceive value or failure; personalization should be added only where data and operational capability support it.
Transformation requires evidence of changed customer or societal outcomes, not just a nicer interaction.
